content:
According to a recent Bloomberg report, Apple is conducting layoffs across multiple teams. Overall, the company has cut more than 200 positions across its Vision Pro, Siri, and software engineering teams.

An Apple spokesperson said in a statement that the adjustments are meant to "advance the business and deliver the best experience for users."

The report says the Vision Pro team accounts for roughly 100 of the layoffs. Among them, Apple is "significantly dissolving a Vision Pro team focused on gaming," while also reducing the size of the team responsible for producing immersive video content for Vision Pro.

Looking ahead, Apple still plans to "produce a smaller volume of content in-house," while encouraging third-party developers to create immersive content.

The report continued:

Additionally, Apple also cut approximately 100 positions from its Siri and software teams.

The report says the Siri team restructuring is related to the rollout of Siri AI. Apple's new-generation Siri AI platform is built on a revamped technical architecture, which has changed the "expertise" required by the Siri team. As a result, Apple has decided to "streamline a small number of existing roles, reassign resources, and add new positions to support the all-new Siri."

Apple's "Intelligent Systems Experience team" has also been affected by this round of layoffs.

Bloomberg's report today builds on an earlier report that said Apple had cut around 60 employees from the Vision Pro team.
